what_it_is: Chinese security vendor with NSFAIS suite: AI-SCAN, AI-UTM, AI Guardrails, AI-DR and AI red teaming.
identity_note: NSFOCUS (nsfocusglobal.com). Scope: NSFAIS AI security series.

1.reason: Agent asset system inventories models, tools, MCP and knowledge bases. AI-SCAN finds exposed OpenClaw hosts by IP range.
1.evidence: discovery and dynamic inventory of core AI agent components
1.has: AI Agent Asset and Risk Governance System, AI-SCAN host and component vulnerability scanning.
1.lacks: No stated multi-cloud inventory. No CI/CD checks. Shadow AI evidence is thin.

2.reason: Runtime protection monitors MCP and tool interactions and auto-blocks unauthorized access. AI-DR adds agent permission control.
2.evidence: monitor real-time interactions with MCP, tools, and external systems
2.has: Agent runtime protection blocks unauthorized MCP and tool access. AI-DR released September 2026.
2.lacks: No named managed agent platforms. No host or kernel sandbox.

3.reason: Runtime agent protection detects and auto-blocks risks. AI-DR launched September 2026. SIEM and SOC links not documented.
3.evidence: AI Agent Detection and Response (AI-DR), released in September 2026
3.has: AI-DR and agent runtime protection detect and block unauthorized agent actions.
3.lacks: No cloud control-plane log source, named SIEM or ITSM integration, or host blocking.

4.reason: AI-UTM gateway blocks prompt attacks and masks sensitive data in LLM inputs and outputs.
4.evidence: AI-UTM is deployed in front of the API interface of the LLM service
4.has: AI-UTM gateway, AI Guardrails, three-level content filter and DLP above 99% accuracy.
4.lacks: Gateway and reverse-proxy modes only. Output filter covers illegal content, not hallucination or code.

5.reason: AI-SCAN assesses against OWASP Top 10 for LLM and regulatory content rules. AI-UTM keeps a full-link audit.
5.evidence: Supports full-link security audit of intelligent agent applications and LLM API input and output.
5.has: AI-SCAN risk reports, OWASP LLM assessment, AI-SBOM guidance, AI-UTM full-link audit.
5.lacks: No product AIBOM export. NIST, ISO 42001 and EU AI Act mapping not shown.

6.reason: AI-SCAN runs 100,000+ test cases and 21 attack types. AI Red Teaming runs multi-round dialogue attacks on agents.
6.evidence: simulate 21 types of attack methods such as prompt word injection and data poisoning
6.has: AI-SCAN attack library and AI Red Team Assessment and Continuous Validation Platform.
6.lacks: No scheduled or CI/CD runs documented. Framework mapping limited to OWASP LLM Top 10.

7.reason: AI-DR does agent identity recognition and permission management. AI Security Gateway handles authentication, authorization and token control.
7.evidence: asset discovery, identity recognition, permission management, and behavioral governance
7.has: AI-DR agent identity and permissions, gateway key and token control, plaintext credential detection.
7.lacks: No per-agent cryptographic identity. No per-tool policy detail. NHI governance limited.

8.reason: AI-SCAN scans 15+ model file formats for backdoors. Skill packages get AST static analysis.
8.evidence: covering backdoor risk detection in 15+ mainstream AI model file formats
8.has: AI-SCAN model backdoor scan, 3,000+ component vulnerabilities and OpenClaw skill AST scan.
8.lacks: Only .pb and .h5 formats named. Dataset checks and AST scope are limited.

notes: Scope read: NSFOCUS NSFAIS series (AI-SCAN, AI-UTM, AI Guardrails or AI-GR, AI-DR, AI Red Teaming, AI Security Gateway) from nsfocusglobal.com. AI-DR (AI Agent Detection and Response) was released in September 2026. Gartner placed NSFOCUS in the Specialists quadrant of the AI Application Security Emerging Market Quadrant (report dated 2026-09-14). No acquisition or rebrand found. Many pages are translated from Chinese and some claims come from solution-method posts, not product datasheets, so detail is thinner than for US vendors. Modules 5.1 and 8.2 rely on a solution blog that lists AI-SBOM and corpus assurance as layers, so both stay partial. The AI-SCAN OpenClaw scan covers gateway exposure, plaintext credentials, memory poisoning and skill supply chain, with a 576-entry malicious skill list. Less sure: 2.1 (no managed platform named after extra searches), 6.3 (continuous validation claimed, scheduling and CI/CD not shown), 8.1 (15+ formats claimed, only .pb and .h5 named), 4.2 (jailbreak not named, prompt attacks and DLP are).
